user.title: Connect to EMHASS
user.description:
EMHASS Companion drives an existing EMHASS installation. Version {min_version} or newer is required.

If you run the EMHASS add-on, the address below is filled in for you.

data_description.url: For example http://localhost:5000, or the add-on's internal address.

price.title: Electricity prices
price.description:
Only sources you have installed are listed.

{profiles}

tariff.title: Buy and sell prices
tariff.description:
Your price source provides raw spot prices. Add whatever your supplier and grid operator charge on top, and what you are paid for exports.

Use **Linear** for VAT plus a fixed markup per kWh, **Already includes costs** if your price source already adds them, or **Template** for tiered or time-of-day pricing.

data_description.buy_multiplier: Multiplied with the spot price. Use 1.25 for 25% VAT.
data_description.buy_adder: Added after the multiplier. Grid fees, energy tax, supplier markup.
data_description.buy_template: Only used in Template mode. `spot` and `time` are available.
data_description.sell_adder: Added after the multiplier. Any per-kWh export compensation.
data_description.sell_template: Only used in Template mode. `spot` and `time` are available.

pv.title: Solar forecast
pv.description:
Choose where the PV production forecast comes from. Pick **No solar** if you have no panels.

{profiles}

load.title: House consumption
load.description:
How EMHASS should predict your household's baseline consumption.

{profiles}

battery.title: Battery
battery.description: Leave this off if you have no home battery. Everything else on this page is then ignored.

data_description.soc_min: As a fraction. 0.10 means the optimiser will not plan below 10%.
data_description.soc_target: Where the optimiser aims to leave the battery at the end of the horizon.
data_description.soc_entity: Read at the start of every run so the plan starts from reality.

grid.title: Grid connection and schedule
grid.description: Your connection limits, and how often the plan is recalculated.

data_description.optimization_time_step: Finer resolution captures more price detail but makes the optimisation slower. 30 minutes suits most homes.
data_description.dayahead_fallback_time: A full day-ahead plan is normally rebuilt automatically as soon as new prices arrive. This time is only used as a backstop if that never happens.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach EMHASS at that address. Check that it is running and that the address and port are correct.
error.unknown_version: Connected, but EMHASS did not report its version. It is probably too old.
error.version_too_old: This EMHASS is too old. Version {min_version} or newer is required, because this integration reads the plan through the JSON API introduced in that release.

abort.no_profiles: No usable data sources were found. This is unexpected; please report it.

inverter.title: Battery control
inverter.description:
How the battery is actually commanded. Leave this unset and the integration only ever reads — the plan is yours to act on however you like.

Nothing is written to your hardware until you also turn on the Control enabled switch.

emhass_version_unsupported.title: EMHASS is too old
emhass_version_unsupported.description: EMHASS Companion needs version {required} or newer, but version {installed} is installed. It reads the optimisation plan through the JSON API added in {required}. Update the EMHASS add-on or container, then reload this integration.

invalid_profile.title: {count} data source profile(s) could not be loaded

run_dayahead.name: Rebuild day-ahead plan
run_dayahead.description: Runs a full day-ahead optimisation over the whole planning horizon.

run_mpc.name: Recalculate now
run_mpc.description: Runs a model-predictive optimisation from the current state.

test_profile.name: Test a data source profile
test_profile.description: Resolves a profile and returns what it produced, for diagnosing a source that returns nothing or the wrong values.

options.name: Options
options.description: Options to resolve the profile with. Defaults to the configured ones.

limit.name: Limit
limit.description: How many series entries to include in the response.

user.title: Add a deferrable load
user.description: A load whose timing the optimiser may choose: a dishwasher, a car charger, a pool pump. Things you change day to day become controls on the load's own page once it is added.

data.name: Name
data.single_constant: Must run in one unbroken block

data_description.nominal_power_w: Roughly what this load draws while it is on.
data_description.operating_hours: How long it needs to run in total. The optimiser chooses when.
data_description.earliest_start: Only used if you turn on the load's time window switch afterwards.
data_description.latest_end: May be earlier than the start time, for an overnight window.
data_description.semi_continuous: On for a dishwasher or pump, which are either on or off. Off for something whose power can be varied, such as a car charger.
data_description.single_constant: On if interrupting it would be a problem, such as a wash cycle.
data_description.startup_penalty: Discourages switching on and off repeatedly. Leave at zero unless that is a problem.
data_description.power_sensor: Optional but recommended. Lets the optimiser know the load is already running, so it is not charged a start-up cost twice or asked to repeat work it has already done today.
data_description.control_entity: Optional. If set, the integration switches this on and off to follow the plan, once you enable control. Leave empty to keep control in your own automations.
